nodes.summary: If a side of the edge `{a, b}` is the pair `{x, y}`, then `a` is a common neighbor of the leaves `ι x` and `ι y`: they form a cherry.
nodes.title: A two-taxon side forms a cherry

nodes.summary: The path length between two taxa is half the sum, over the darts (oriented edges) of the tree, of the lengths of the edges whose split separates them.
nodes.title: Split decomposition of a tree metric

nodes.summary: A side holding a single taxon `z` is the leaf side of `z`'s pendant edge.
nodes.title: A singleton side is a pendant leaf side

nodes.summary: On the path-length metric of a binary phylogenetic `X`-tree with positive edge lengths and at least four taxa, any pair of clusters that neighbor joining may join from the initial singletons consists of two taxa with a common neighbor.
nodes.title: The first join of neighbor joining on a tree metric joins a cherry

nodes.summary: (Saitou & Nei 1987; Studier & Keppler 1988; Bryant 2005). Let `d` be the path-length metric of a binary phylogenetic `X`-tree `(G, ι)` with positive edge lengths `w` and at least four taxa. If the distinct taxa `x, y` minimize the Q-criterion over all pairs of distinct singleton clusters at the start of neighbor joining, then `ι x` and `ι y` have a common neighbor.
nodes.title: On a tree metric, a pair of taxa minimizing the Q-criterion is a cherry

nodes.summary: For a compatible system of splits with positive weights, containing every trivial split and binary (every side with at least two taxa is the disjoint union of two sides), on at least four taxa, a pair maximizing the total `splitGain` is a side of some split.
nodes.title: Cherry lemma for split systems

nodes.summary: Let `S` partition the taxa of a binary phylogenetic `X`-tree `(G, ι)` with positive edge lengths `w` and path-length metric `d` into sides of edges. Then there is a system of splits `A e` (`e : E`) of the set of clusters with positive weights `w' e`, closed under complement, pairwise compatible, binary, and containing every trivial split, such that edge with both endpoints internal; splits separating `s` from `t`,…
nodes.title: The path metric on a partition into sides

nodes.summary: The dissimilarity between clusters at the start of neighbor joining: on singletons, `initialDist d {x} {y} = d x y` (only singleton values are used).
nodes.title: Initial cluster dissimilarity in neighbor joining

nodes.summary: `G` with the taxon placement `ι` is a binary phylogenetic `X`-tree: `G` is a tree, `ι` is injective, the leaves (degree-one vertices) are exactly the taxa, and every other vertex has degree three.
nodes.title: Binary phylogenetic tree

nodes.summary: The cluster dissimilarity after joining `a` and `b`: the new cluster `a ∪ b` is at `(D a c + D b c - D a b) / 2` from every other cluster `c`, and at `0` from itself; other values are unchanged.
nodes.title: Cluster dissimilarity after a neighbor-joining step

nodes.summary: Let `(G, ι)` be a binary phylogenetic `X`-tree and `D` any dissimilarity. Suppose that whenever a run of neighbor joining on `D` has reached a partition `S` of the taxa into sides of edges of the tree (with at least four clusters) and joins two of its clusters, their union is again a side of an edge. Then every complete run of neighbor joining on `D` (stopped with at most three clusters) forms exactly the splits of…
nodes.title: Neighbor joining forms the splits of a tree when every join forms a side

nodes.summary: Let `d` be the path-length metric of a binary phylogenetic `X`-tree `(G, ι)` with positive edge lengths `w`. Then every complete run of neighbor joining (stopped with at most three clusters) forms exactly the splits of the internal edges of the tree: a set of taxa `A` or its complement is a formed cluster if and only if `A` is the set of taxa on the `a`-side of an edge `{a, b}` with both endpoints internal.
nodes.title: Neighbor joining is exact on tree metrics

nodes.summary: `NJRun d S D C`: some run of neighbor joining on the dissimilarity `d` reaches the cluster set `S` with cluster dissimilarity `D`, having formed the clusters in `C`. A join is allowed while at least four clusters remain, for any pair of distinct clusters minimizing `qCriterion`.
nodes.title: Runs of neighbor joining

nodes.summary: The Q-criterion of two singleton clusters at the start of neighbor joining: `Q({x}, {y}) = (|X| - 2) d x y - ∑_z d x z - ∑_z d y z`.
nodes.title: Q-criterion of two singleton clusters

nodes.summary: The Studier–Keppler form of the neighbor-joining criterion on the cluster set `S`: `Q(a, b) = (|S| - 2) D a b - ∑_{c ∈ S} D a c - ∑_{c ∈ S} D b c`.
nodes.title: Neighbor-joining Q-criterion

nodes.summary: In a tree, the splits of any two edges are compatible: one side of the first edge lies inside one side of the second.
nodes.title: Splits of two tree edges are compatible

nodes.summary: At an internal vertex `a` with neighbor `b`, the `a`-side of `{a, b}` is the disjoint union of the far sides of the other two edges at `a`.
nodes.title: Edge side at an internal vertex as a disjoint union

nodes.summary: The leaf side of a pendant edge holds only the leaf's taxon.
nodes.title: Leaf side of a pendant edge

nodes.summary: Every side of every edge of a binary phylogenetic tree holds a taxon.
nodes.title: Every edge side of a binary phylogenetic tree is nonempty

nodes.summary: In a tree, the two sides of an edge partition the taxa.
nodes.title: Two sides of a tree edge partition the taxa

nodes.summary: The taxa on the `a`-side of the edge `{a, b}`: those whose vertex is still joined to `a` once the edge `{a, b}` is deleted.
nodes.title: Taxa on one side of a tree edge

nodes.summary: The contribution of one split `{A, Aᶜ}` to the neighbor-joining score of the pair `x, y`: the number of taxa on the far side of the split when `x, y` lie on the same side, and `1` when the split separates them.
nodes.title: Contribution of a split to the neighbor-joining score

nodes.summary: If `d x y` is half the total weight of the splits `A e` separating `x` and `y`, then `(|X| - 2) d x y - ∑_z d x z - ∑_z d y z = -∑ e, w e * splitGain (A e) x y`.
nodes.title: The Q-criterion of a split-decomposed dissimilarity

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
